# jailoc

> jailoc is a Go CLI tool that runs coding agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, OmO) in sandboxed micro-VMs. Each workspace boots its own libkrun VM with directory shares for project paths, a userspace network broker that blocks private networks, and SSH-based agent sessions.

Key facts:

- Every workspace is a per-workspace libkrun micro-VM; `jailoc-guest` is the VM init and agent sessions run over SSH into the guest
- Supported hosts: macOS on Apple Silicon (Hypervisor.framework) and Linux amd64 (KVM, `/dev/kvm` access required); jailoc downloads a pinned, SHA-256-verified VM runtime
- Workspace images are built with Docker Engine on the host (or in a builder VM with `isolated_build`) and exported into the VM root filesystem
- All guest traffic passes through a host-side network broker: public destinations are allowed, private and reserved IPv4/IPv6 ranges are denied unless listed in `allowed_hosts` or `allowed_networks`
- Config lives at `~/.config/jailoc/config.toml` (TOML); persistent VM home state lives under `~/.cache/jailoc-vm/workspaces/<workspace>/home`
- `jailoc migrate` converts a jailoc v1 (Docker) configuration

## Reference

- [CLI Reference](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/reference/cli/): Root command (`--new`, `--attach`, `-c`, `-s`, `-w`) and all subcommands (`up`, `down --purge`, `restart`, `reload`, `sessions`, `logs`, `traffic`, `strace`, `exec`, `shell`, `status`, `add`, `config`, `migrate`) with flags
- [Configuration Reference](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/reference/configuration/): Every `config.toml` field in `[base]`, `[vm]`, `[defaults]` and `[workspaces.<name>]`, with types, defaults, validation rules and merge semantics; built-in coding agents with their session flags, persistent directories and environment
- [Image Resolution](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/reference/image-resolution/): How the workspace image is chosen, built and exported into the VM
- [Default Image Contents](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/reference/default-image/): Tools and runtimes shipped in the embedded base image
- [Overlay Compatibility](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/reference/overlay-compatibility/): Rules for workspace Dockerfile overlays

## How-to Guides

- [Installation](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/installation/): host requirements, pre-built binaries, building from source, VM runtime
- [Workspace Configuration](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/workspace-configuration/): Add workspaces, set paths, mounts, snapshots, ports and per-workspace options
- [Custom Images](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/custom-images/): URL Dockerfile presets, local Dockerfiles, build context, isolated builds
- [Network Access](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/network-access/): allowed_hosts, allowed_networks, filtered DNS, verifying the policy
- [Secrets](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/secrets/): Pass secrets from host environment variables (from_env), files (from_file) or commands such as password managers (from_command) into the VM as session environment variables or /run/secrets files; rotate with reload
- [SSH & Git Passthrough](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/ssh-git-passthrough/): Forward the SSH agent and known_hosts, copy Git config into the VM
- [Sessions](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/sessions/): Attach to, start, continue and list agent sessions; read logs
- [Coding Agents](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/coding-agents/): Choose OpenCode, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI or OmO per workspace, run several agents on one project, log in, pass arguments, install the agent yourself
- [TUI Plugin](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/tui-plugin/): Enable the TUI sidebar plugin to show workspace context in the OpenCode sidebar
- [Migrate from jailoc v1](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/migrate-from-v1/): Convert a Docker-based configuration with `jailoc migrate`
- [Troubleshooting](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/how-to/troubleshooting/): Find logs, debug common errors, clean up stale state

## Explanation

- [Overview](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/explanation/overview/): Startup sequence and package layout
- [Threat Model](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/explanation/threat-model/): What jailoc protects against and what it does not
- [Architecture](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/explanation/architecture/): Builder and workspace VMs, image export, jailoc-guest init, SSH sessions, virtio-fs shares, persistent home, Docker inside the VM
- [Network Isolation](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/explanation/network-isolation/): Userspace network broker, IPv4 and IPv6 policy, filtered DNS
- [Secrets Architecture](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/explanation/secrets/): Destination and source secret mapping, delivery over SSH, tmpfs storage in the guest

## Optional

- [Getting Started Tutorial](https://seznam.github.io/jailoc/tutorials/getting-started/): Step-by-step walkthrough for first-time users
